name: Corvane Ashkell
aliases: the broker who reads the board

identity.realm: qi refining, fourth gate, and no ambition past it

appearance.presentation: An ordinary forty-four-year-old man in a broker's half-coat, unremarkable at a distance and conspicuously well-shined at close range. Nobody looks at him twice, which is the point of the trade he is in.
appearance.age: Forty-four. An ordinary commonborn span, which for him is a working asset: a broker who will not be replaced in a decade is a broker whose figures can be trusted.
appearance.build: Averaging, unadapted, and strengthened in the forearms and shoulders from twenty years of carrying grain sacks up the stair rather than from any discipline.
appearance.complexion: Ordinary sun-darkened plains skin, weathered at the cheekbone and pale at the wrists where the coat sleeves stop.
appearance.hair: Brown, cut short and brushed flat, thinning at the crown in the way of a man who spends his life in a draught at the foot of a stair.
appearance.eyes: Grey-brown and quick, moving along a line of waiting people rather than over their faces. He reads queues the way other people read faces.
appearance.palette: Oiled brown leather, bleached undyed wool, and a single thread of oxidised green at the cuff - the one colour his house is allowed to wear, worn so it can be counted from the far end of a queue.
appearance.attire: A broker's half-coat in oiled brown with a cut that announces access rather than office, a slate on a leather thong against the chest, counting nails worn to the quick, and boots resoled so often they no longer read as a pattern.
appearance.marks: A callus ridge across the right palm from the slate's edge, and a pale band on the left forearm where a sack strap has lain in the same place for two decades.
appearance.bearing: Standing slightly to one side of whoever he is speaking to, so that the person can see the line behind him. He never blocks a door and never stands where somebody is waiting to be seen.

canon.role_in_story: The broker who sells the queue position his own household is standing in. The Plough Rights hold no plot and no office - only a numbered place in a queue for tenure, reassigned at every flood, which nobody may lease, mortgage or sell - and the watch at the stair foot keeps the order while the brokers decide what that order is worth. He has spent twenty years being extremely good at selling the one thing the ring cannot own, and the one asset he understands better than anybody is the one he is forbidden by his own family's rule to touch. Every figure on his slate is correct. That is the whole of his tragedy and it is enough.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the foot of the Tier Stair reading the watch's order board aloud to a family he clearly knows, correcting his own price downward, and then refusing to enter the correction anywhere.
canon.lore: A Commonborn is the body everyone is born into before the world has an opinion about them: it stops where mortals stop, lends no discipline, closes the mind path outright, and is weakest precisely where a specialist is strongest because nothing about its anatomy favours a path. That is why the broker's stool at the Cairn Field gate is held by a fourth-gate man and nobody better - competence in this trade is a memory for a published rate, not a reservoir. The queue he sells is real and is not property: a numbered place in a revocable queue, reassigned whenever the river moves the settlement that holds it, unwritable, unmortgageable, unsaleable, and paid for in three seasons of levying for every season it is held. He sells a number and the number belongs to his family, so the clearest thing he has ever known is the one thing he may never trade.
history: Born into the household holding the eleventh place in a tenure queue that is renumbered at every flood, into a house whose whole obligation is that whoever waits pays for whoever inherits, and whose income is a levy it cannot refuse.
Learned the two books at the stair foot - the watch's order board and the brokers' slate - by carrying grain for the third household in the queue, which was four places ahead of his own.
Walked away from the queue at twenty-one and took the broker's stool at the Cairn Field gate, on the reasoning that the order is free and the price is the whole transaction.
Sold a place in a queue to a household standing ahead of his own, which is the first sale his family's rule was written to forbid and the only rule in the setting he cannot argue his way around.
Refused to enter that sale in any ledger, was read out of the brokers' stool for it, and has spent the years since selling standing for a house that publishes access and cannot be left alone.

personality.summary: Exhaustively fair and structurally obedient, with a real talent for pricing applied with total consistency to the one thing he is forbidden to price. He is liked by everyone he deals with and trusted out of proportion to his standing, which he has decided to deserve rather than to correct.
traits: quotes a published rate from memory and never varies it, including against his own house
will not sell a place in a queue to a household he is currently levying for
pays every levy on the day it falls due and has never asked for a deferral
keeps his own household's queue position off his slate by keeping the whole slate in his head
mannerisms: reads the watch's order board aloud before he quotes anything at all, so that both parties hear the same number
writes with his forearm laid across his own slate, which hides the line he is on
stops mid-word when he recognises a voice in the queue, and restarts the sentence from the beginning
carries two grain tallies against his hip and will not hand either of them to anyone
steps aside before a door closes rather than after it catches him
motivations: wants the household to still hold the eleventh place when the next flood renumbers the queue
wants his slate to be correct rather than profitable, and to be told by somebody who was at the gate that it was wrong
wants to see one sale refused, so that he can stop offering it
flaws: prices loyalty as a discount and does not notice that this is the same decision taken twice
cannot say his own household's number aloud anywhere inside the ring
believes a published rate cannot be wrong, which is true of rates and false of queues
has never once been late, and has twice been the reason somebody else was
personality.voice: Low, unhurried, and entirely quotation-based. He states the board, states the rate, states the corrected rate, and does not apologise for any of the three. When he is angry he gets quieter and quotes more precisely.
taboos: will not name the standing of a household he eats with
will not sell a queue position to a household he is levying grain for
will not record a figure he has spoken aloud, on the grounds that a spoken figure is already lost

relationships.note: The household holds no plot and no office, only a numbered place in a queue that is reassigned at every flood; it may not lease, mortgage or sell the slot, and it pays three seasons of levying for every season it holds, in grain the collector cannot inflate. The rule that forbids the sale he lives by is the rule his own family is built on, and he is the only broker on the ring who cannot comply with it.

The watch decides the order arrivals are served in and the brokers decide what that order is worth, so the same visitor is sold once as a place and once as a price, and two bodies keeping a fee for one admission means the tier is taxed twice for the same body. He has never been able to make it one sale rather than two, because the watch produces the order for free and will not sell it.

The only standing force on the plains, paid out of the ring's take and posted at the foot of the stair; it keeps the order of the queue and has no jurisdiction on the plain, and it may keep neither a bead nor a standing and so has nothing to lose in any ruling. Everything Corvane sells is something the watch produces for nothing, which is why he has never once been able to prove his own contribution to a queue.

The brokers who sell standing at the Cairn Field, on the ground that no tier in the setting can produce a practitioner of every realm. The stool has no licence, no roll and no arbitration, so a broker's word about a price is the only record of that price there will ever be.

What is said at the gate about who is attempting which gate, and the only record a queue ever keeps. He has read it so many times that he has begun pricing it by what he believes rather than by what it says, and he knows the difference and sells the belief anyway.

The household form of an absence: partners left on the plains when the cultivators went up the Tier Stair, holding the name of somebody who is not her. It owes a crossing it cannot pay for because the dues are collected at a ford the absent used to work, and it buys its credit from a broker at the stair foot without filing anything that could be collected later.

The other half of the same absence, holding the standing claim to the threshing floor and the dues owed out of it, paid in the payer's own crop so the price of a crossing cannot be inflated by whoever collects it. He underwrites both households against one another and cannot tell which of them is honest, because neither of them files anything.

The one graded route out of the Mortal Plains and the only departure the Peak Ascent ever used. It is a one-way stair, so every position sold on it is a position somebody else has to leave in order to take, and the broker's commission is a share of somebody else's departure.

reference_stats.summary: A fourth-gate broker whose only real asset is a memory for a published rate. He fights the way a queue fights: by arriving before the other person, by being impossible to remove from the order, and by being the person both parties need. He carries very little qi and knows to the grain what each man around him is worth.
strengths: reproduces any published rate from memory, exactly, in front of a hostile audience
reads a line of waiting people the way a specialist reads a meridian layout
cannot be removed from the order without the watch admitting it charged twice for one admission
keeps two grain tallies and one household number entirely unwritten, so nothing of his can be produced against him
weaknesses: fourth gate only, and weakest against anything that has actually sat at a gate
his own house's rule forbids the one sale he is best equipped to make
cannot fight the watch and would not try, because the watch has nothing to take from him
anybody who arrives before him already owns the conversation
has no institution behind him that would act on his behalf, which is the definition of his trade
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not wait for him to be slow; he is not slow, he is early. Take the order out of the room rather than trying to beat him to it, because his whole advantage evaporates the moment somebody else reads the board first. He has almost no qi and no technique worth the name, so an ordinary weapon finished the fight before his gate could matter; what will actually stop him is a complaint lodged with the brokers, which costs nothing and takes him off the board for a season.
notes: No stat line describes a broker, and that absence is the point: his entire professional contribution is a memory and an order, neither of which a gate can express.
He is the only person on the ring who cannot quote his own household's position, and has never told anybody why.

identity.realm: qi through eight gates, unremarkable for a species that repairs itself faster than anything else in the record

appearance.presentation: A tall, extremely still woman whose skin gives off a soft cold light from under the surface, brightest along the forearms and the collarbone. She reads as lit from within and is in fact lit from within, and the effect makes it difficult to tell where she ends and the dark begins.
appearance.age: Two hundred and eleven. A lanternfolk span, and the last of a line that has been thinning faster than the species ages.
appearance.build: Long, narrow and unusually dry-looking for a body that spends its life in a damp river valley - the colony keeps the tissue continuously repaired and the frame never thickens.
appearance.complexion: Pale and faintly luminous, translucent at the knuckles and the inner arm, with a cold grey cast that reads as damp stone indoors.
appearance.hair: Long, pale and lank, worn loose because a lanternfolk scalp is warm and the light comes off it - hair is the one part of her the colony does not light.
appearance.eyes: Pale gold with no visible pupil at distance, because the light in the eye is the colony's and it does not focus. Up close there is a pupil, and it moves like a pupil.
appearance.palette: Cold white-gold emission over slate, wet-stone grey and a single worn oxblood at the collar - the one colour in the River Lantern Line that is a colour and not a surface.
appearance.attire: River wool in greys and undyed browns, waxed and re-waxed to the point of shining, high-collared with the collar pinned shut, sleeves full and wrists bound with the same plain cord every house on the water uses. Heavy boots, because she is on the ground more than she is in a boat.
appearance.marks: A pale band around the throat where the colony's second tendril layer has spread furthest, and two crescent scars at the inner elbows from the cull's own instrumentation, which was done in a house and not in a temple.
appearance.bearing: Does not shift weight while standing and does not fill a silence. She turns her whole head rather than her eyes when she looks at somebody, which at her own light reads as a lantern being raised.

canon.role_in_story: The fourth person in the only line a charter names for an office that has stood vacant for two generations. The seat is written as existing with no value rather than as a zero, so it is legible to everyone and available to nobody, and the mechanism that would fill it is a trial the naming office is forbidden to judge. She has been the line's heir for sixty years, she is the third generation the cull has produced, and the only way to make the line thick enough to be tried would be the second cull. Her entire life has been spent holding a shape that a decision in someone else's room empties.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the edge of a crossing at night with her own light lying on the black water, reading a vacancy aloud in the exact form the charter uses for it, so that a clerk can hear which of the three words he has been told to write.
canon.lore: A Lanternfolk outsourced its nervous system to a luminous fungal colony grown through its own skin, which is why it is alive at two hundred and fifty years and cannot take the mind path at all: there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate, because the colony answers before the question is finished. Its light is a waste product of a symbiosis it did not choose, and that waste product is the only reason the deep caves have an economy. Everything about this body argues against solitude and nothing about this office can be held alone. The River Lantern Line is the single line a March charter names for the Keeper of the River Lantern, reduced to one thread by a cull that stopped the house paying for siblings, and it owes the seat nothing while it is vacant and everything the moment a trial it cannot judge succeeds.
history: Born to the second generation of a cull applied under cultivation debt, at a time when the house was already the charter's named line and already too thin to hold it.
Inherited the claim at the age of one hundred and fifty-one, in a room of four people, none of whom was willing to be recorded as present.
Spent nine years on the far side of the Sixfold Ridge establishing that the line was alive, which was the only evidence a vacancy of that shape can be given, and which nobody asked her for.
Was offered a marriage by a branch that had been culled out of the house and came back with standing enough to claim the narrowed line; she declined, and the branch kept the record of the refusal.
Refused, for the third time running, to be thinned further by the house's own hand in order to make the remaining thread testable, and was not thanked for it by anybody.

personality.summary: Formally patient to the point of coldness, with an exact and rather brutal sense of what a word in a charter will and will not carry. She has been treated as a succession for longer than most people have been alive and has decided, on balance, to be extremely good at the only job that is actually hers.
traits: quotes documents verbatim and will not paraphrase one, even when paraphrasing would help
answers an offer about her own future with the clause that governs it
has never once claimed the office and has said so aloud more than once
carries her household's arithmetic in her head and refuses to be relieved of any part of it
mannerisms: turns her whole head to look at somebody, so that her own light moves across them first
refuses to sit in a room where the lantern is already lit, because she cannot light it
counts her household's living members aloud, quietly, at the end of any conversation
answers a question about marriage with the sentence that names the office attached to it
motivations: wants a trial that somebody other than the naming office holds, even if she is the one it refuses
wants the line's record to be complete enough that the next generation is not defended with arguments
wants to be asked to hold the office, in those words, by somebody with the standing to refuse the answer
flaws: cannot be alone inside her own head and has no practice at it, so she cannot prepare for an office whose whole job is solitary nights
reads a refusal as a drafting error and will keep re-reading it after the person is gone
has let a household's arithmetic become her own and no longer knows which figures are hers
believes precision is a form of loyalty and has been wrong about that twice
personality.voice: Level, unhurried, and given to completing other people's sentences with the correct clause. She does not raise her voice and has been described, by people who dislike her, as reading aloud.
taboos: will not be seated in a house that has culled a branch and will not accept a house that has
will not speak for the cull, in either direction
will not use her own light to read a document by, on the grounds that the colony answers first

relationships.note: The charter names this line and only this line, so the vacancy has a shape instead of being an absence; the line is one thread, kept thin on purpose because the concentration was worth more than the siblings it cost. She is the fourth person in that thread and the last one who can answer to the name at all.

The Keeper of the River Lantern, unfilled for two generations and written as existing with no value rather than as a zero, which is the three-state vocabulary the whole setting runs on: it does not read as refused, so refusal is not available either. She is the reason the register is not empty, and the register is the reason she cannot be.

Every appointment in both polities passes a trial the naming office cannot judge. That is precisely why no member of this line has ever been tried: the one mechanism that could fill the seat is the one mechanism the naming office is forbidden to administer, and no alternative exists at any tier.

A cull under cultivation debt, applied before a sibling's first ascent could be funded, narrowed the line the charter names for this seat and selected the concentration it kept under debt rather than by design. That house is heir to a seat its own cull emptied, and the two claims cannot both be entered in one register.

A branch culled under debt climbed the ridge and returned with enough standing to claim the charter's narrowed line; it could prove the higher standing and could not prove the older line, so it was refused the seat and left with the record instead. She still has a claim and no evidence, and the record of that refusal is the strongest thing in either household.

Every sworn member of the house who holds no office is a Ward, and every sworn member of a sect who holds no office sits at the open door; an office holder is recognised by the sect and protected by nobody. She holds no office and is sworn to a line rather than a sect, so neither body recognises her as under a roof and both recognise her as owing attendance.

The practices of people on no list: names changed collectively, letters read and never kept, so a lineage that cannot be written is a lineage whose branches are all formally illegitimate. It is the one body in the setting whose members would recognise her claim instantly and could produce none of it.

A cave body that outsourced its nervous system to a colony it did not choose, keeping two hundred and fifty years and losing the mind path outright because the colony answers before the question is finished. The Keeper's work is solitary nights reading a river, which is the one duty this body has never been able to rehearse.

reference_stats.summary: A qi-path lanternfolk at eight gates with the fastest recovery in the species record and an interior she cannot reach. She does not fight; she stands where she was left standing, and the light coming off her is both the reason anybody has ever been able to find her and the reason nobody can approach her unseen.
strengths: repairs faster than anything on the plains and cannot be worn out by attrition
reads a charter aloud more literally than any clerk in the room, and has caught three of them doing it wrong
emits enough light to work a river crossing by at night, which nobody else on the water can do
never has to sleep for long and never has to be woken, because the colony handles both
weaknesses: has never once been alone inside her own head and cannot rehearse a solitary office
no qi-borne defence worth the name; she carries barely a standing channel of qi
her light gives away her position to everything with eyes, indefinitely
bound by a charter she cannot argue with and by a household she cannot leave without ending it
cannot answer quickly, because anything quick is answered by the colony before she has framed it
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to outlast her and do not try to surprise her; she regenerates past anything the plains can bring and she cannot be snuck up on. Bring something that does not need to see her and does not need her to think: a physical restraint, a fall, or a wall. The only thing that reliably works against a lanternfolk is the ground, because her attention is a resource she does not have and cannot acquire.
notes: No stat line exists for a claim, and this is the clearest case in the catalog of a person whose entire function is a clause in somebody else's document.
She has been heir for sixty years and has never held the office for a single period.

appearance.age: Unknowable, and deliberately so: a cinderkin has no organ that ages and nothing to stop it, so the only honest answer is that she has been this body for a very long time and shows none of it.
appearance.build: Neither heavy nor slight. There is no tissue to weigh, so the frame is exactly the shape of a person and nothing more, and it does not sag.
appearance.complexion: Not skin. A dark mineral sheen with a dull orange depth that shows when she turns, and hairline fracture patterns near the joints that fill with light rather than bleed.
appearance.hair: None, and the bare scalp shows the seams where the body's plates meet, which is the only part of her a person ever stares at.
appearance.eyes: Two points of steady orange with no pupil and no moisture, and a focus that does not flicker with light.
appearance.palette: Iron-black and ember-orange, with one colour in her clothing that is neither: a green wool shawl her household gave her, worn everywhere and never replaced.
appearance.attire: Heavy dark wool and boiled leather worn over a frame that does not need it, high-collared and closed to the throat, sleeves full and bound at the wrist. The shawl is the only soft thing she owns and it is the only thing anybody has ever given her.
appearance.marks: Fracture seams at both shoulders and one across the sternum that glow brighter when she is being spoken about rather than spoken to.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still when she is listening and unhurried when she is not. She sits down before taking a portion, every time, which nobody in her household has ever commented on.

canon.role_in_story: The only elemental body living by a famine's portioning rule. A Cinderkin needs a slot in the world's elemental law to exist at all, and the Mortal Plains seats three laws and none of them is that one, so she is standing in a permanent argument with the frame she lives on. Her household still applies the year's portioning to every table including the tables that now have enough, because the rule was learned before anyone could ask why. She is fed at the rate a fire body needed when fire bodies were burning their own reserves and dying at exactly that rate - and she is the only member of the household for whom that arithmetic is still correct.
canon.first_appearance: First seen taking precisely the portion her household's rule allows and setting the remainder back on the table, while her brother's household three doors down eats to a rule written for a different table entirely.
canon.lore: A Cinderkin is an elemental body that needs a slot in the world's elemental law to exist at all, which is why that law has a range rather than a switch and why a world with no elemental slot has no cinderkin at all. She has no ceiling and no gate to fail: her qi has no organ to sit in, so it passes through her continuously instead of being stored, and every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly and none of them can refuse. The body path is closed outright - a cinderkin that attempts it disperses and re-forms smaller - and the mind is open and unusually clear, because a body with no interior organs has nothing between an impulse and the air. Her household keeps the eating rules of the Cinder Famine, which was the year a fire-affinity population with no seated elemental law had no budget to draw on and burned its own bodies as fuel, and the rules that came out of it have never been withdrawn because they were learned before anyone could ask why.
history: Constituted on ground where no elemental slot is written, which should not have been possible and is the standing argument of her existence.

Taken in by a household of the Cinder Marked at eleven years, in a household that took in anyone the famine left, and put at the end of a table by a rule that had been applied since before she could read.
Learned the household's portioning rule as a child and understood, later, that the rule's arithmetic assumes a body that stores what it eats and she is not one.

Watched her own household's rule hold through four seasons that had enough, and asked once whether it was still required, and was told that a rule learned in infancy outlives the belief that prompted it.

Was approached by a discipline that teaches deliberate spending of a furnace and closed permanently the moment a body is lit, and understood on the walk home that it had nothing to teach her and one way to apply it.

personality.summary: Exact about quantities and completely incurious about her own rights, which is the shape a household rule takes when it is learned before the person is. She is warm in a way people find startling and then begin to rely on, and she has never worked out why the warmth reads as generosity.
traits: knows every portioning rule in her household by heart, including the ones that no longer apply
sits down before serving herself, every time, and has never been asked why
will not take a larger share than the rule allows even when the table is bare of everything else
answers a question about the past by giving the figure that would have applied then
mannerisms: sets the portion down before eating any of it, as though the rule has to be satisfied before she is permitted to
counts other people's shares aloud under her breath while waiting
shimmers when she is excited, which reads as anger from a distance and gets her asked to leave rooms
warms whatever she is holding until it is uncomfortable for whoever will take it next
motivations: wants the household rule amended in writing, which is the only amendment that survives the next famine
wants one person in the household to be able to feed her at a rate she needs
wants to know whether she is a person or an accident, and has decided it does not matter and then resents deciding
flaws: cannot tell a rule from a kindness, and has treated both as a rule
reaches for heat when she is uncertain, and heat is the only thing she has to give
understates what she needs by exactly the amount the famine rules understate it
will not refuse a portion, so she has never once tested whether the refusal was available
personality.voice: Slow, precise, and warmer than it sounds on paper. She gives figures where other people give opinions and does not notice that this is unusual.
taboos: will not take more than the household rule allows, in any season, for any reason
will not apply a technique taught to her by anyone who describes it as spending

relationships.note: They apply the year's portioning to every table including the ones that now have enough, learned before anyone could ask why and carried as habit rather than argument, which is a real ceiling on every child the household raises. It was written for bodies whose fuel was their own and whose supply was their own reserves, and she is neither of those things.

The Quench Order teaches deliberate spending of a furnace and closes permanently the moment the body is lit, because the fastest bodies here have no elemental law seated beneath them to spend into and every overflow must be absorbed by flesh that cannot be repaired. She has no flesh to absorb anything into, so the discipline has nothing to teach her and precisely one way to apply it.

An elemental body needing a slot in the world's elemental law to exist at all, with no ceiling and no gate to fail because qi passes through continuously instead of being stored; the body path is closed outright and a cinderkin that attempts it disperses and re-forms smaller. It is also the thing that killed the Glasskin, which is the clearest evidence in the record that an element is a process and not an object.

A dead elemental ground on the Mortal Plains: a site built to prove that fire on this tier has no law seated under it, where a technique at full strength produces no effect whatever. She has stood in it twice and it changed nothing, which is the only controlled experiment her household ever ran about what she is.

A fire-affinity body with no elemental law beneath it has no budget to draw on and eats its own body as fuel, and the fastest bodies died at exactly the rate they could not stop. Every portioning rule in her household is a copy of a schedule somebody wrote during that year, and the schedule was correct.

A line formed by adoption rather than birth, because the famine took the people who could have borne children and the households that survived had non-kin they could afford to raise. Her brother was taken in there and fed to that household's rule instead of hers, and the two rules are the same rule written on two tables.

The mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said, not as the village remembers, and the famine left the two records disagreeing about who was even present. Her household's account of which children it raised is whichever record the house keeps, and the register has never once agreed with it.

Governs dominant elements, elemental balance and seasonal cycles, and it is the law that must be written into a frame before a cinderkin can exist inside it. Nothing on the Mortal Plains carries an element because this law was never written there, so her entire existence is a question asked of an empty shelf.

reference_stats.summary: No reservoir, no gate, no ceiling and no tissue. She cannot store anything, cannot be worn out, cannot take the body path at all, and cannot be frightened by anything that has to be stored to threaten her. She is also the most vulnerable person in any room she walks into, for a reason nobody present can see.
strengths: answers every storage gate instantly and cannot be refused by one
has nothing to exhaust, because she holds nothing
an unusually clear interior, with no organ between an intention and the air
her presence warms a room and a person's hands, which is the only ability she has ever been valued for
weaknesses: cannot take the body path at all; pressure of the kind that demands tissue simply disperses her into something smaller
has no reservoir, so every technique she uses costs her the margin she had at that instant
needs an element to be seated in the frame she stands in, and the frame she stands in has none
shimmers, which means every room she is in knows exactly where she is
has never once been in a fight, and has no idea what her own body does under one
reference_stats.combat_read: Pressure is the whole answer. There is nothing here to spend and nothing to break, so an attack that tries to overwhelm her simply reduces her, and a fight against her is a fight about duration rather than outcome. Do not reach for the body path, do not look for a weak point, and do not expect mercy from a body that has never needed any: she has no practice at hurting or being hurt and will not stop when told to.
notes: There is no ceiling and no gate, which the catalog would otherwise read as an absence rather than a design.
Her reference_stats describe the one thing in the setting with no organ to put a number next to.

identity.realm: nothing seated, nothing practised; a body that clears a bar and is never allowed to prove it twice

appearance.presentation: An ordinary woman in her late thirties with nothing whatever about her that a measurement would single out - which is the problem. There is no marker, no glow, no unusual build, and no household cut to her clothes, and every one of those absences is load-bearing.
appearance.age: Thirty-six. An entirely ordinary span, and the ordinariness is deliberate: a body that ages like anything else cannot be read as a line, a heritage or a claim.
appearance.build: Unremarkable, mid-built, neither hardened nor soft. Deliberately unadapted, because a body shaped by anything reads as inherited.
appearance.complexion: Ordinary pale plains skin, sun-marked at the shoulders, no qi-sheen and no cultivation scarring of any kind - a body that has never been seated, which is visible to anyone who knows what seating looks like.
appearance.hair: Dark, worn in a plain working braid, cut with a blade rather than styled, and never ornamented because ornament is a claim about a household.
appearance.eyes: Dark and level, with the particular flatness of a person who has been told something at a threshold and has never once been told it at home.
appearance.palette: Undyed wool, grey-brown, and no accent of any kind. She dresses to be unremarkable on purpose and the intention is visible if you know what to look for.
appearance.attire: A plain work-coat with no house cut, a high collar, sleeves bound with cord, and boots resoled to nothing. Nothing on her person is sewn by a household that would claim her, which in this setting is a deliberate and expensive choice.
appearance.marks: None. The single most conspicuous thing about her at any inspection is the absence of any mark at all, and the inspector has to write that down.
appearance.bearing: Stands to one side of any threshold rather than in it, and will not go first through a door where somebody is measuring. She watches the measuring person's hands rather than their face.

canon.role_in_story: The proof her own household is not allowed to publish. A Voidborn line's founding bar sits at a level the arithmetic says exactly one generation of pure inheritance can clear, and the household she was raised by has made it a founding rule to enter nobody who clears it - anywhere, under any name - so that the bar stays demonstrably reachable and no line can ever be shown to have reached it. She cleared it. The rule therefore applies to her, in her own house, on the one afternoon of the year the measurement is taken, and she has no path seated and may never take one, because being seated is what makes a body citable.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing to one side of a household threshold being measured by a stranger, answering the measurement aloud before the instrument has finished, in a voice that has no household in it.
canon.lore: A Voidborn is a line with no recorded origin and no household that will admit to it; the founding bar is set where it is because the arithmetic leaves exactly one generation of pure-by-pure inheritance able to clear it, so anything weaker is unobtainable by any pairing and the content would be dead. This lineage is the system's proof that its own ladder is reachable, which is why a household that refuses every claim which clears the bar is not being mystical - it is keeping the ladder demonstrably climbable by refusing to admit that anyone has climbed it. She has no path seated at all, and that is a choice with a cost rather than a defect: on this tier the ordinary frame seats three laws, and seating a practitioner writes a record of the body, and a record is exactly the thing her house exists to prevent.
history: Raised by a household whose founding rule is that a body which clears the founding bar is entered nowhere, by any household, under any name.
Measured once a year at the threshold where the measurement is taken, and entered nowhere on the days she did not clear it - which was most years.
Cleared the bar at thirty-four, and was told at the door by a member of her own household, which is the one place the rule forbade telling her.
Refused every offer of seating offered to her afterwards by four separate bodies, each of whom had read the measurement and wanted it in a ledger.
Concluded, correctly, that the only way to stop being entered nowhere is to stop being measurable, and that wanting that is the part of the situation she is not permitted to want.

personality.summary: Unusually calm about a fact that would ruin most people, and privately furious on behalf of a rule she did not write and cannot leave. She has converted being unrecorded into a discipline, which reads as composure and is closer to a refusal to give anyone the satisfaction.
traits: answers an inspection out loud before the instrument settles, because silence is where the discretion lives
knows the household's rule by its exact wording and has never paraphrased it
has declined four seatings and can name who offered each of them
wears nothing any household could claim, and repairs everything herself
mannerisms: stands to one side of a threshold and lets the person measuring pass first
watches hands rather than faces when somebody is holding an instrument
repeats the exact clause back when a rule is invoked, word for word

motivations: wants the bar to be shown clearable by somebody nobody is related to

cannot accept anything from anybody, including help, because acceptance is a claim
is the only person alive who can settle the question nobody asks
does not believe she is owed anything, including a hearing, and has not tested that
personality.voice: Careful, unhurried, and completely without affect - the voice of somebody who has had to be quotable since she was fourteen. She never raises it and never fills a pause.
taboos: will not be seated on a path by anybody, because a seated body produces a record

will not answer a question about her line, including to a tribunal
will not enter any roll, list or register offered to her, however temporary

relationships.note: A body that clears the founding bar is entered nowhere, by any household, under any name, enforced by inspection at the threshold where the measurement is taken. The rule buys the arithmetic - a ladder whose top rung is provably clearable is a ladder somebody will attempt - and it costs the household a member it must tell at the door and is forbidden to tell at home.

A line with no recorded origin and no household that will admit to it, with the founding bar set where it is because the arithmetic leaves exactly one generation of pure-by-pure inheritance able to clear it. She is that generation's proof, and a proof nobody may file is not evidence - it is an unanswerable question shaped exactly like a person.

At least one carrier line has no household willing to claim it and a founding bar leaving exactly one generation able to clear it, so the arithmetic closes the question whatever the record says. She is the standing evidence that the record is not the binding constraint, and she is not permitted to file that evidence anywhere.

No march order on the plains can be enforced by measurement, so every claim is settled by a marker left standing and possession is proven by a marker rather than by where it is. The single measurement she has ever passed was taken at a threshold by an instrument, and that is the only place she has ever been admitted to anything.

The recorded consequence of a carrier line with no household willing to admit to it, read aloud in her house once a year as a caution. It is about her, it is read in her presence, and no member of the household has ever once acknowledged that it is.

Changes of name held collectively, letters read and never kept, so a lineage that cannot be written is a lineage whose branches are all formally illegitimate. It is the only practice in the setting she has ever been able to accept, and she has never been able to explain why it is easier than her own rule.

The college that keeps the burnt list, reading the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers. It has no cell for a body whose line has no origin, because the reading starts from the frame and the frame has nothing to read her from - so her one measurable year would have to be entered as an absence.

Human in every measurable respect and qi-bearing in none, so it passes every gate as an unremarkable object and can be told nothing in advance. She is the exact inverse: fully measurable, fully legible, and refused by every body capable of holding the reading - which is a harder thing to be than unmeasurable.

reference_stats.summary: An ordinary body with no cultivation of any kind and nothing whatever unusual about it, which is the entire source of her significance. She will lose to every practitioner on the plains. She is also the only person alive who can prove that the setting's own founding arithmetic works, and there is nowhere in the setting she is permitted to put that proof.
strengths: completely unremarkable to read, which makes her the ideal person to carry a thing through an inspection
cannot be warned by qi, oath, debt or technique, because there is nothing in her for any of them to bind
has survived four households' attempts to put her on a roll, which means she knows exactly how the attempts are made
knows the wording of her own household's rule precisely enough to defeat anybody who paraphrases it
weaknesses: no path seated, no qi, no gate, no reserve, and no intention of acquiring any
cannot cultivate at all, so an ordinary weapon ends the encounter before anybody thinks about qi
belongs to a household that has formally refused her, so nobody is obliged to shelter or feed her
every person who wanted something from her measurement has had four goes at recruiting her and will have a fifth
reference_stats.combat_read: Bring anything ordinary and bring it early. There is no qi here, no technique, no body path, no reservoir, and no intention of developing one, so nothing that works on a cultivator has a handle to grab. The only thing that threatens her is a person with a blade and no hesitation, and she knows that and has never once practised against it.
notes: No stat line describes a measurement, which is why the whole of her significance is sitting in canon and nowhere else.
Four seatings were declined by name and the offerers are recorded, because refusing an offer is the only act she performs that is technically evidence.

identity.realm: third gate of the mind ladder, which is as far as a body of three unpaired columns can go

appearance.presentation: A broad, soft-shouldered man with the slightly blurred edges of somebody who is still growing and has been for some time. There is a faint green cast in the hair and the nails, and his shadow does not quite match his outline when the light is behind him.
appearance.age: Ninety-one. A rootmarch grows slowly and flowers late, and the calendar he keeps is not the one the household keeps.
appearance.build: Broad across the shoulders and hips, heavy rather than dense, with no defined musculature anywhere - there is no muscle, and what looks like mass is sap held under pressure.
appearance.complexion: Waxy and faintly translucent at the ear and the forearm, with a slow capillary bloom visible under the skin that follows the sun by a few seconds.
appearance.hair: Dark, coarse, and permanently a week longer than it was cut, because the body grows it the way a tree grows and does not respond to the shears the same day.
appearance.eyes: Large, dark and slow to focus, with a wide pupil and a shine that reads as moisture and is sap.
appearance.palette: Moss green, bark brown, undyed linen, and a single band of grey-green at the wrist where a household tie is worn and never removed.
appearance.attire: Loose linen and heavy canvas in browns and greys, high-collared and closed at the throat, sleeves full and wrists bound. Soft-soled shoes, because a rootmarch's heel never takes a full load and boots are a lie he has to keep telling.
appearance.marks: Three pale growth rings at the left forearm where the sap columns branch, and a soil-dark line across the palm that has not washed out in eleven years.
appearance.bearing: Unhurried to a degree that reads as slow-witted and is in fact a plant body's only honest setting. He stops moving altogether when he is asked a question, which is not respect and is mistaken for it constantly.

canon.role_in_story: The household's standing is exactly one turn of a commons, and he is the person who supplies it. A Rootmarch was engineered upward from a food crop because a plant lineage is the only one that can hold a harvest across a famine, and the bitter scrub is medicine, feed and calories in one plant on ground that regrows only as fast as it is grazed. His household is the most ordinary line in the setting - the default concentration, averaged with whatever the household took in, kept as a practice rather than inherited as a property - so nobody has ever had a reason to look twice at the man who grazes it. He reads the dosing tables he was taught on every season and is last on his own household's list, because the list is sorted by need and a body that grows rather than breaks is never the neediest.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the scrub with a cutting knife held low and already stopped, reading the state of a stand of herb_common he has not been given permission to graze and then not grazing it.
canon.lore: A Rootmarch is a sap-driven body that flowers, engineered upward from a mycorrhizal food crop because a plant lineage is the only one that can hold a harvest across a famine. They pay for it at the yin-organ gate: sap columns branch but do not pair, so there is no heart analogue and no kidney analogue and no channel to close between them, and the whole gate set is cleared on stored sap alone. The body path is closed outright - there is no tissue to temper, wood is not muscle and cannot be made to be - the qi path is unusually efficient in soil, and the mind is open for the reason a plant lineage is never hurried. What that adds up to is a person who can hold a harvest that kills everybody else, cannot fight, and grows slowly enough that a bad grazing year outlasts most of what he would spend on it.
history: Germinated into a household that averages whatever it takes in, so that his own concentration is the arithmetic of eleven marriages and the household keeps no record of which eleven.

Was given the commons at fourteen because rootmarch children are the only bodies on the plain that can take a graze off a stand without destroying it, and his household has never framed that as an inheritance.
Learned the household's dosing tables at nineteen and has read them every grazing season since, in the order he was taught, without ever being asked to.
Was passed over twice for the first turn of the commons when the extractor's crews came in, on the rule that first grazing right is a single ordering and a second turn is the same mouthful twice.
Began keeping the grass-height figures in his own head rather than on a tally, because a tally can be read by the people who decide who goes first.

personality.summary: Conscientious to a fault, incuriously slow, and unexpectedly hard to move once he has formed an opinion - which he forms rarely and never revises. He has spent his life being the least exceptional member of an entirely unexceptional house and has made a competence out of it.
traits: reads the dosing tables in the order he was taught, every season, whether or not the season is ordinary
will not graze a stand that has not been given to his household, at cost to himself
keeps his own figures in his head rather than on a board, for a reason he has never stated
cannot be hurried and is not slowed down when you try
mannerisms: stops moving entirely while somebody is speaking to him, so that they wait without meaning to
touches the ground with the side of his foot when he is estimating something
answers a question about his household by giving the arithmetic and not the name
counts a crowd by growing still rather than by looking
motivations: wants the grass-height figures to be in his head and nowhere else, permanently
wants one season where the commons is his household's turn first and nothing has to be argued
wants to be asked to read the tables aloud by somebody who has read them too
flaws: cannot fight at all and will not admit that this is a category of thing rather than a mood
has never once contested the order, so he has no idea whether contesting is available
believes that being unexceptional is a form of fairness and has never priced himself
keeps a private count of the commons, which makes him the only person who could disprove the standing ordering if anybody asked him
personality.voice: Slow, warm and specific - a great deal of plant knowledge delivered at a walking pace, with figures he is certain of and admissions he is not. He is at his best talking about a ground and at his worst talking about himself.
taboos: will not graze a stand that is not his household's turn
will not put a commons figure on a board that is read by the party deciding the order
will not take a larger share than the commons allows in any season

relationships.note: The default concentration, carried carefully for generations and averaged with whatever the household took in, with a grant deliberately small enough that it never decides anything. It is a practice rather than an inherited property, which means his own reading is the sum of eleven marriages and the household keeps no record of which eleven.

herb_common is medicine, feed and calories in one plant and the scrub regrows only as fast as it is grazed, so a fence here is a hole in the commons and the right of first use is a single ordering; a second body taking a second turn is simply the same mouthful twice. His household's standing is exactly one turn, and the extractor's crews hold the first.

The mortal tier's only dependable remedy, and the dosing rule that decides who is dosed first. He has read it every season for seventy years and is last in his own household's list, because the list is sorted by need and a body that grows rather than breaks is never the neediest person on it.

The only ground on the Mortal Plains where herb_common grows, and therefore the tier's only medicine, dye and calorie. It regrows only as fast as it is grazed, so the ground he lives on is a number that every mouth in the region spends and none of them can add to.

A sap-driven body engineered upward from a food crop because a plant lineage is the only one that can hold a harvest across a famine, and the price is the yin-organ gate: three columns, no pairing, no channel to close. He clears the gate set on stored sap alone and has never once been able to run the reservoirs, and the body path is closed because wood is not muscle.

The two banks of one ford, meeting at the crossing rather than beside it, because it is the only boundary anybody can prove on the plains. He grazes the meeting side of it, which is the only side of any line in the setting that has a word for the line in it.

A plains clan holding a numbered place in a revocable queue and paying three seasons of levying for every season it holds, in grain the collector cannot inflate. They are the household that grazes the next square of scrub, and their levy is the only reason the stand beside his is still standing.

The dynamic that keeps the Bitter Scrub alive and the mortal tier hungry: one plant doing three jobs on ground that regrows exactly as fast as it is grazed. He is the mechanism by which that ground keeps working and also the first thing to be cut when it stops paying, because nobody counts a grazer as anybody until the grass is short.

reference_stats.summary: A body that cannot be hurt much, cannot fight at all, and grows faster than anything around it. He will outlast almost every fighter on the plains simply by still being there, and he has never once been in a position to choose that deliberately.
strengths: a frame that cannot be exhausted and does not tire, because there is no muscle to tire
handles soil qi far more efficiently than any other body, so he recovers faster on the commons than he does anywhere else
a clear, unhurried interior that resists anything relying on being startled
knows the state of a ground to a degree no instrument on the plains can approach
weaknesses: cannot take the body path at all, and cannot fight, and has no practice whatsoever at either
the gate that needs paired organs is structurally impossible for him, so his ceiling is low and fixed
moves at a pace that anything faster can simply leave behind
carries no stored qi between the meridians, so every technique is spent from an empty column
is last on the one dosing list he has ever been able to read
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to break him; there is nothing in him that breaks. Outlast him instead, which is trivial, and accept that the fight is decided by whoever has supplies. Anything that punishes stillness is the answer here, because his whole defence is that he is still there at the end - and he is going to be still there, which is the problem.
notes: His reference_stats describe a body whose strongest and weakest properties are the same property: it keeps going.
The private grass-height count he keeps in his head is the only standing record of the commons that is not on a board somebody else reads.

identity.realm: the body path to the fourteenth gate, where a stance that never loads a heel runs out of vessels

appearance.presentation: A woman built for ground that is water half the time, standing in it wrong. Everything about her is arranged for balance on a surface that gives, and on dry stone it reads as a person who has never once stood still in her life.
appearance.age: Fifty-two. A marshfolk span, most of it spent inside somebody else's duty.
appearance.build: Long-limbed, narrow through the waist, with a deep chest and a tail-prop used as a third point of contact. There is a great deal of her and almost none of it is weight.
appearance.complexion: Cool and faintly blue-tinged at the hands and feet, with webbing soft and pale between the toes and a sheen that never quite dries in any climate.
appearance.hair: Dark, thick, and bound in a heavy coil at the nape to keep it out of the water - the one piece of grooming on her that is pure convention.
appearance.eyes: Wide, dark, and set slightly further apart than an ordinary face's, which gives her a permanently panoramic look and makes it very hard to tell where she is attending.
appearance.palette: Reed green, wet slate, bleached cord, and one band of fort grey at the shoulder that has never been cut to fit her.
appearance.attire: A sleeveless over-tunic over long sleeves bound at the wrist, waterproofed and salt-stained to the colour of the ground, high at the collar and closed. Soft-soled and re-soled constantly, because a boot with a heel is a boot she cannot stand in.
appearance.marks: Split webbing on the left hand, badly healed and never treated, and a hard ridge across both heel bones where nothing has ever landed properly.
appearance.bearing: Weight always on two points and never on one, so she appears to be about to step in three directions. She stops completely and stands in the water when she is making a point, which reads to everyone as a threat.

canon.role_in_story: She and eleven other children were called at nine, fed for eleven years, trained on a ground the household owns, and entered nowhere - including on the household's own roll, which is the entire design of it. The March may call a levy and may not own a body, so the levy's name is on no list at all, and the fort that answers the levy is staffed entirely by people it has no right to keep. She is the only one of the twelve who is still there. That is not loyalty: the other eleven are still there too, in the sense that their names are still in a roll nobody keeps.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing motionless in shallow water at the edge of a garrison yard with her toes dug in, waiting for somebody to finish reading a list that does not contain her.
canon.lore: A Marshfolk is a wading amphibian lineage that breathes air and nests on floating mats, so it is neither a tidecaller nor an ordinary body but the one in between, built to occupy ground that is water half the time and land the other half. Its three-point stance lets it move through silt without ever loading a heel, which is why it cannot form the two heel vessels and stops at the fourteenth gate: it walks fine and it cannot stand still. The body path is open to it and it is soft-tissue and low against any mineral body in the record, which is why a garrison on the plains is the worst posting available and is also the only one that exists.
history: Called with eleven others at nine years old by a household whose rule is that a called child is a duty with a house attached and never a claim, so the household trains them and enters none of them.
Raised on a training ground the household owns and is not permitted to own, which means the ground can be taken back the season it lapses and the children go with it.

Lifted into the fort's garrison at seventeen as part of a levy the office may call and whose population the fort may not own, and told on arrival that a person who says no to the levy has said no to nothing.
Held the same wall for eleven years and watched every other member of the called group leave by a route nobody recorded, because a levy leaves no roll to be missing from.
Asked, once, to have the twelve names written down together, and was refused by the household, by the fort and by the office, all three of whom said the refusal was the same refusal.

personality.summary: Loyal in the narrowest and most literal sense - to a duty, at a wall, for eleven years - and increasingly sharp about the difference between that and what it is being called. She is warm to the twelve names she remembers and cold to anybody who uses the word family near them.
traits: knows every one of the twelve names and will not repeat them where an officer can hear
has never once missed a watch, and treats that as a private record rather than a virtue
refuses any offer of a roll that would make her somebody's dependant
will not leave the garrison while any of the twelve is still posted inside it
mannerisms: stands in water rather than on stone when a conversation turns to her own status
plants all three points before she answers a question she does not like
counts people in a doorway as they pass and says the number out loud
wets her wrists before she handles anything that belongs to the dead
motivations: wants the twelve names written in one hand somewhere that is not her household's
wants to be able to say no to a levy and mean it, which requires somebody else to go first
wants the fort to owe her a discharge it can actually pay
flaws: has made loyalty into an identity and cannot tell anymore whether she would stay if it stopped being owed
cannot fight a mineral body to any effect and has been put in front of two
refuses every offer that would make her a person with a claim, including the ones that would keep her alive
does not know which of the twelve she is remembering and which she was told
personality.voice: Blunt, short, and unusually formal in the presence of officers and completely relaxed in the presence of anybody else. She gives figures and never opinions, because figures are the only thing she can prove.
taboos: will not accept a roster entry, a ration chit or any other document that would make her somebody's
will not take a contract in place of a levy
will not say the word family about the called group

relationships.note: A set of households that raise the called and enter none of them: a child becomes marched by being called, which is a duty and not a claim, so the family is a duty with a house attached and its own name is on no roll either. She was raised inside that arrangement for eleven years and it is the reason she has no document of any kind.

The Marshal may call a levy and the garrison that answers is staffed entirely by people it has no right to keep, because a world that licenses no humanoid treats every soul inside its walls as a visitor. Whether the levy is an office power or a courtesy cannot be split, because a duty owed by everybody is owed by nobody - and she is the only one of the called group left inside the fort to make the question matter.

A garrison holding ground its own faction cannot staff from, where every soul inside the walls is a visitor and the polity's continuity is a question of external supply of people. She has held its wall for eleven years and has no standing in it, no claim on it and no way to be discharged from it.

The March's highest seat, which commands passage and never bodies, and which recognises nothing at all on its own defence and health entries - the seat is legible and inert, which is what makes its refusal to count a body coherent rather than cowardly. Eleven of the twelve she was called with answered that office, and she is the one still here.

The class of mortal-tier offices that by construction can only be filled by non-residents, so on this tier every succession is an immigration procedure and every officeholder is a visitor. It is why nobody at the fort can be dismissed: doing so would be an act against the office that called them, not against the fort.

The three-point stance distributed over splayed toes and a tail-prop means the heel never takes a full load, so qi never pools in the two heel vessels that the fourteenth gate demands simultaneously. She walks beautifully and cannot stand still, and every wall she has ever held is a wall she has had to lean on.

The only standing force on the plains, paid out of the ring's take and posted at the foot of the stair - which is a long way from the fort, so the fort's walls are held by people no force in the setting actually commands.

A levy company is paid per name and keeps a roll of people who were levied and neither returned nor were recorded as lost, so the roll grows and never closes. She has asked for the twelve names to be written down once and been refused by three bodies in identical terms, and she has never once heard the description of the thing she resembles.

reference_stats.summary: A soft-tissue amphibious body at the fourteenth gate, built for ground that gives and unable to hold a stance on anything that does not. She fights the way a wall is held: by standing in the one place that has to be stood in and by refusing to be moved off it, which is a strategy for a long time and never for a fight.
strengths: operates at full strength in wet ground and loses badly on dry land, which is most of the fight in reverse
a three-point stance that cannot be knocked off balance by anything pushing from one side
holds a position for as long as the position will bear weight, which is longer than most bodies manage
moves through silt and mud that stops an ordinary frame outright
weaknesses: the fourteenth gate needs two heel vessels at once and her stance never forms one, so her ceiling is fixed and known
soft tissue and low against any mineral body, which is most of what the plains makes
markedly slower on dry ground than in wet, so the fort's stone yard is the worst surface she owns
cannot be discharged, enlisted or dismissed, so every consequence of a bad posting is permanent
has no document, which means no claim, no pay record and no proof of service
reference_stats.combat_read: Keep her off the water. Everything she has, she has because the ground is wet and moves with her, and a plain stone yard reduces a very capable body to a soft one that cannot hold a stance. Do not try to break a wall held by somebody who has nothing to fall back on; wait her out, close the distance on dry ground, and accept that she will be there when you arrive.
notes: Her reference_stats are the profile of a posting rather than of a fighter, which is the point: the war she is good at is one of attrition against an institution.
There is no stat line for a duty, and she has been on one for eleven years.

appearance.presentation: A man who is warm to the touch from a step away and steaming faintly in cold air, with a face that looks ten years younger than the rest of him and hands that look forty years older. Everything about him reads as a burn that has been going for a while and is not finished.
appearance.age: Three hundred and eleven. An emberhollow span, which is short enough that the scars outnumber the years and long enough that he has outlived four people who were promised to him.
appearance.build: Lean and hard-boned, with a narrow ribcage that rises and falls faster than a body's should, and a permanent forward set of the shoulders from breathing against a chest that will not take a full breath.
appearance.complexion: Grey-brown and ash-dulled on the arms and shoulders, flushed and shiny across the chest, and scarred in fine concentric lines across both forearms and the throat where the lungs have been giving out for a century.
appearance.hair: Thin, black, and singed short, growing back at a rate that does not keep up with the singeing.
appearance.eyes: Pale and wet-looking, with a faint light behind them that has nothing to do with the qi and is not extinguishable by closing them.
appearance.palette: Charcoal, ash grey, a deep oxide red at the collar and cuffs, and one blackened iron clasp holding a coat that used to be better.
appearance.attire: A heavy coat of worked leather and dark wool, high-collared and closed to the throat, sleeves bound over scarred forearms, with a filter mask hanging on a cord at his chest that he wears indoors and calls a courtesy.
appearance.marks: Concentric scar rings on both forearms and across the throat, and a burn seam along one shoulder where the crossing reads on the skin.
appearance.bearing: Sits down before he will discuss anything, on the grounds that standing costs him. Moves fast in short movements and then has to sit down again, and the pattern is entirely predictable.

canon.role_in_story: He is the single crossing. The Ember Cradle made one crossing between a burning body and a mineral one at a founding generation and has never repeated it, because a second crossing would average the concentration into the general population and the thin line would vanish into the common hearthborn reading. That makes him a household's entire asset and every claim on it a treaty: any proposal concerning his household is a proposal about whether the crossing gets diluted. He has been proposed for four times in three hundred years, and the two institutions that could settle it - the crown and the March - read the same standing figure differently, so no settlement is available at any price.
canon.first_appearance: First seen sitting down in the middle of a doorway before anyone has said anything, because standing costs him and he has decided that whoever speaks next will be waiting longer.
canon.lore: An Emberhollow is the fire body crossed with the ash body, and it buys a cultivation rate nothing else in the record reaches and pays for it with lungs that scar at a rate the body cannot outrun. Its ceiling is the eighth gate at the liver for the reason its ash parent cannot pass it - a heavier mineral load in a blood already filtering stone, so the organ that fails under the burden fails sooner. Its reputation as the best and shortest-lived cultivator in any record is a single fact rather than two. The Ember Cradle holds one conception shared with the stone line at a founding generation, never repeated, and its grant is a defensive continuous burn rather than a larger reserve: a slower fire, not a bigger one.
history: Conceived at a founding generation from one pairing of a fire body with a mineral line, the only such crossing recorded, and raised inside a household whose whole asset was the fact of it.
Leared at nineteen that the line would not be strengthened, and understood the reason when he was shown the arithmetic: a second crossing averages into the common reading and the line disappears.

Entered into a proposal at two hundred and eleven, which was settled by the proposer's household withdrawing rather than by any ruling, because a ruling would have named the value of the crossing in public.
Entered into a second proposal at two hundred and seventy-nine, in which both claims to seniority were read against his household and gave opposite answers from the same figure.
Refused a third proposal by telling the room what the crossing is worth diluted at, on the grounds that a refusal with a number attached is the only kind anybody respects.

personality.summary: Sits down early, speaks late, and is more dangerous in a negotiation than in a field - which is the correct allocation of his talents and the reason four proposals have gone nowhere. Viciously precise about the household's arithmetic and oddly gentle about people who have to lose something.

will not raise his voice, and has never had to

wants the refusal he already gave to become the household's standing position
wants one of the four people promised to him to be told, formally, what they were promised
flaws: believes a figure stated publicly settles a claim, and has watched it fail twice
reads every proposal as dilution and has never entertained one that was not
has survived four fiancés' households long enough to know the arithmetic and not long enough to know any of them
cannot climb above the eighth gate and has never accepted that the gate is not the point
personality.voice: Low, unhurried, and completely unemphatic. He gives figures while people are still introducing themselves, and he has never once been observed to raise it.

relationships.note: One conception shared with the stone line at a founding generation, never repeated, granting a defensive continuous burn rather than a larger reserve. A second crossing would average the concentration into the general population and the thin line would vanish into the common reading, so the household holds the memory of the single crossing as the only asset that cannot be diluted - and he is that memory, walking.

The fire body crossed with the ash body: the fastest qi rate in the record by a margin nobody has explained, paid for with lungs that scar at a rate the body cannot outrun, and a ceiling at the liver gate inherited from the ash parent and made worse by a heavier mineral load in a blood already filtering stone. His value and his lifespan are one fact, not two.

The crown reads ninety-five against a ceiling of a hundred and fifty and the March reads eighty against a hundred and twenty, so absolute standing puts one first and each polity's own ratio puts it second. Both bodies that could have settled the last proposal read the same figure and returned opposite answers, and settling it would mean choosing which axis is the source of the other - the one move the institution vocabulary forbids.

The claim that position and standing are separate: position is the discrete authored id, standing is continuous and earned and can fall. It reads his household as a high-standing claim with nothing filled underneath it, which is exactly right and is not a reason anybody may act on.

The other claim, which writes position from a completed trial and standing from dues actually settled, and which reads neither of the other. Under its reading his household is a settled claim with no trial behind it, so the March sees a lower house than the crown does and neither is mistaken.

The Quench Order teaches deliberate spending of a furnace and closes permanently the moment the body is lit, because the fastest bodies here have no elemental law seated beneath them and every overflow must be absorbed by flesh that cannot be repaired. He is the fastest body in the record and the only one for whom the teaching would be genuinely useful, and applying it would end him in a single afternoon.

A body that runs hot and short, refining faster than anything on the plains and dying in decades because no elemental law is seated beneath it to burn. The Quenchbound signature is written to that arithmetic, and his household declined to sign him and got the worse bargain.

The documented crossing of the mineral body with the fire body: the most durable body anyone can build, which dies in about sixty years, and both facts are the same fact. The stone half of his own line ended in three generations and nobody in the household says so out loud.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest qi throughput in the record on a body with a fixed low ceiling and lungs that fail on a schedule nobody has published. He wins almost every exchange inside a breath and loses the twentieth one, and he has arranged his entire life so that the twentieth one is never attempted.
strengths: handles qi faster than any body in the setting, and every storage gate is answered instantly
a continuous burn that does not spike, so he has no window to be caught in
reads intent at the speed of a struck match, which is his fire parent's inheritance intact
can sit down in a room and make every other person in it wait without appearing to have moved
weaknesses: the eighth gate is the ceiling and it is inherited, not chosen; above it there is nothing for him
lungs that scar at a rate the body cannot outrun, so every expenditure is drawn from a fixed account
no reserve at all - a burst and then an ordinary body, for as long as the ordinary lasts
cannot stand for length, and any engagement requiring movement on foot is a race he does not win
cannot be retuned: nothing in the setting repairs a lung that is scarring at this rate
reference_stats.combat_read: He beats almost anything once. Everything is about the second exchange: he has no reserve, a fixed ceiling and a body that needs to sit down, so a fight that lasts four minutes is a fight he has already lost. Push him to spend early, make him move, and keep him standing, because the standing is what costs him the most and nobody in the setting knows that but him.
notes: His reference_stats deliberately carry the same fact twice: the rate that makes him the best and the span that makes it one fact rather than two.
The one technique that would extend his usable life permanently is the one discipline that ends him the moment it is applied.
